quote: 109,846 patients from 25 unique studies were included
GLP-1RA reduced the risk of MI, stroke, cardiovascular mortality and MACE in a broad range of patients with and without T2DM and/or prior ASCVD

sec: Methods / Study design and search strategy
quote: This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted with reference to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020. Two electronic databases, Embase and Medline, were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) relating to treatment with GLP-1RA and prevention of MI

Non-randomized controlled trials and observational studies, including cohort and cross-sectional studies, were excluded from this study. Reviews, study protocols, letters, commentaries, conference abstracts were also excluded. Studies in pediatric populations were also excluded in this study
The proportion of males ranged from 24 to 76%, and the mean age was 62.6 ± 9.2 years
Most studies were conducted in a multi-national setting, except for two studies conducted only in Japan
Glucagon like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) use in individuals with high atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk reduces major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE)
Most studies were conducted in patients with T2DM, except for one study conducted in a cohort with obesity in the absence of T2DM
Over a follow-up duration of 3.48 ± 1.51 (1.55 to 5.47) years
Majority of studies compared GLP-1RA to placebo [12, 14, 38–40, 44, 47, 48, 51–61], while others used insulin regiments and other anti-diabetic medications [41–43, 45–47, 49, 50] as the comparators
GLP-1RA reduced the risk of total MI (RR: 0.86, p < 0.01), with numbers needed to benefit (NNTB) of 207 to prevent one event of MI
GLP-1RA reduced cardiovascular mortality (RR: 0.87, p < 0.01, NNTB 170), MACE (RR: 0.87, p < 0.01, NNTB 67) and stroke (RR: 0.88, p < 0.01, NNTB 335) compared to placebo
NNTB 93 (95%CI: NNTB 52 to NNTB 1717, Follow-up time: 3.45 ± 1.21 years) for coronary revascularization
GLP-1RA commonly resulted in gastrointestinal side-effects amongst other systems (RR: 1.55, p < 0.01, NNTH 9)

sec: Methods / Study quality, publication bias and certainty of outcomes
quote: Each study was independently screened by two pairs of authors (FS, JTYH, SKSC, GS). Any discrepancies were resolved by consensus or in consultation with a senior author (ASPT, JQ, YHC, NWC). Quality assessment of included articles was conducted using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (ROB-2) tool
